IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGING - p99 tail latency spike observed for streaming gateway in eu-west2 (p99 ~ 2.9s, p95 ~ 850ms) - impact: some live customers seeing stalls / streaming stalls. Triggered at 2024-06-05T09:12:12Z.
Alice M: seeing the same in dashboards, streaming tails pile up around 1.5-3s, and we have an increase in TLS handshake RTOs in the NAT egress logs.
Ben K: paging oncall - @Oncall Pager can you take? looks like cross-zone traffic to az-b is showing packetloss counters rising.
Oncall Pager: on it - I'm pulling live tcpdump on a few nodes, attaching flow stats.
Carla R: quick question - is this isolated to streaming endpoints or also generation? I see small uptick on normal gen p99 too but less severe.
Alice M: primarily streaming. regen paths seem okay but tails for streaming tails are problematic. Logs show repeated TLS SYN retransmits to remote NAT gateway.
Dave S: can you paste the NAT counters? I suspect ephemeral port churn / conntrack backpressure.
Oncall Pager: here's sample from nat-gw-eu-west2-03: 
```
NAT_EPHEMERAL_EXHAUST=0.75
TCP_RETRANS=312/min
TLS_HANDSHAKE_RTO=0.12%
PKT_LOSS_IFACE=0.7%
```
SRE Pager: interesting - there's also a spike in dns lookup timeouts for our cross-zone resolver (10.8.32.2). Lookup latencies 300-800ms. Could be sticky DNS responses causing some sessions to misroute.
Ben K: ok plan: 1) mitigate customer impact (degraded mode / routing fallback), 2) investigate NAT and DNS path. Alice, can you flip the streaming fallback policy to the lower-latency variant? Use `route: eu-west2-local` and `model_variant: redwood-small` for canary customers.
Alice M: doing an emergency rollout for fallback policy now. Command: `curl -XPOST https://console.internal/api/route/fallback -d '{"env":"prod","region":"eu-west2","variant":"redwood-small","sticky":false}'` 
Alice M: rollout applied to 10% of streaming routes, monitoring.
Carla R: also enabling prefix-KV caching TTL extension to reduce repeated handshakes for the same sessions.
Oncall Pager: I can force local DNS cache invalidation on the Edge nodes to drop stale records: `sudo systemctl restart resolver` on pool eu-west2-edge-*. Doing in rolling batches of 5 nodes.
Dave S: I'm going to add a temporary iptables rule to SNAT outbound to a different NAT pool to avoid the apparent ephemeral pressure. Will do on nat-eu-west2-0[3-4].
SRE Pager: good. Also enabling degraded streaming mode (chunked smaller batches) to reduce per-request connection churn.
Ben K: customer comms: product-ops prepare a short blurb: "Partial streaming interruptions in eu-west2; degraded experience for small percentage of sessions. Working on network mitigations."
Alice M: after rollout to 10% tails p99 on canary dropped from 2.9s -> 1.0s within 4m. Good sign.
Oncall Pager: DNS invalidation completed for first batch of 5 nodes; early telemetry shows fewer DNS timeouts from 300ms->80-120ms.
Dave S: SNAT reassign done for nat-eu-west2-03 -> fallback pool. Conntrack usage down 40% on that gateway. Packet retransmit rates down from 312/min -> 38/min.
Carla R: TLS handshake RTOs trending down. Streaming stalls reduced but still some tail outliers. Might be leftover client-side TCP retransmits from earlier.
SRE Pager: still seeing ~0.1% TLS handshake failure rate, but overall request success returned to >99.5%.
Ben K: Ok next: keep fallback policy at 10% for 10m, then ramp to 50% if stable. Prepare postmortem runbook steps and collect pcap from nat-eu-west2-03 for correlation.
Alice M: started pcap collection: `/tools/pcap/capture --iface eth0 --size 200M --out /tmp/nat03.pcap`
Oncall Pager: I'm handing off to night SRE shift in 30m. @SRE Pager will take followups.
SRE Pager: acknowledged, I'll watch the ramp and keep the runbook steps: 1) confirm conntrack stays < 60%, 2) keep DNS TTL reset across edges, 3) monitor p99 tail for next 2 hours.
Ben K: customer-impact note: two customers saw streaming stalls >20s, but no data loss. ops-slo tag for followup.
Carla R: adding a short repro to the incident; include stack traces and the pcap.
IncidentBot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT UPDATE - mitigations applied (DNS cache flush, SNAT reassignment, degraded-mode rollout). Current severity: P2 (was P1). Next update in 30m or on notable change.
SRE Pager: leaving notes for postmortem: likely combination of NAT ephemeral pressure + stale DNS entries leading to cross-zone pathing to slower NAT gateway; followups: increase NAT pool capacity, add monitoring alert for conntrack >70%, add runbook item to rotate DNS caches on edge on SLO breach.
Ben K: thanks team. handoff complete.
Alice M: marking thread as on-hold under oncall, will update if tails regress. :thumbsup:
